subject: Clarify transient vs persistent retention (request vs outputs)
messages:
From: Sara Turner <sara.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: sec-team@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Default retention and residency — quick Qs

Hi Naomi,

Quick set of questions from our security team while we evaluate Redwood for a PHI-adjacent pilot:

1) By default, what exactly is retained for a regular hosted API request? Is the full request text (prompts) kept, and if so for how long?
2) How do you treat generated outputs — are those stored by default or treated as ephemeral? If stored, what's the retention window?
3) Where are each of those artifacts physically stored (US/EU regions) for a standard hosted account? Can we force EU residency for both requests and outputs?
4) If we opt-out of retention, what breaks (debugging, supportability, billing reconciliation)?

Can you send a one-page summary plus any matrix you have that maps artifact -> default window -> opt-out path? We want to include it in our vendor assessment doc.

Thanks,
Sara Turner
Security Program Lead
Acme Health

Subject: RE: Default retention and residency — quick Qs

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I've attached a concise matrix (retention_matrix_v2.csv) that maps artifacts to default windows and opt-out actions. If you want, we can follow with a short call to walk the security team through the pilot options.

1) What we retain by default (hosted API):
   - Request metadata (timestamps, model id, client_id): retained 180 days for billing and platform telemetry.
   - Full request text (prompts + user message): retained 45 days by default to support debugging, abuse detection, and model-quality regressions. Prompts are treated like request text for classification purposes (customer PII should be treated with the same care).

2) Generated outputs (model responses) — default handling:
   - By default we retain generated outputs for 14 days; these are kept primarily to support session replay and customer-facing debug flows. Outputs are marked as lower-visibility derivative artifacts in our platform.
   - For customers on an enterprise contract we can shorten or entirely disable output retention.

3) Residency:
   - Hosted accounts default to US-backed storage. We offer region-scoped tenancy (EU region) for hosted customers; this can be enabled at signup or during onboarding and applies to requests and outputs for the specified projects.
   - For stricter residency (air-gapped / on-prem) we offer Redwood Private which provides full control over where artifacts land (customer VPC / on-prem storage).

4) Opt-out implications:
   - If you disable request-text retention: we cannot replay requests for debugging, incident triage, or quality regressions tied to that window. Support may require you to reproduce incidents or provide sanitized samples.
   - Disabling output retention removes our ability to provide session replay, and will limit some of the Evaluate/quality tooling. Billing reconciliation still works (metadata remains unless otherwise requested).

Next steps: attached matrix and a short pilot plan (we can land the EU residency flag for your pilot and provide a 30-day retention exception if needed). If that works, I can schedule a 30-45 minute sync with your security folks.

Best,

Naomi — small clarification to keep the external answer tight: our platform-level telemetry (aggregated model metrics, perf traces) is retained independently and doesn't carry user text; that telemetry window is 365 days. Also, for generated outputs the typical hosted default we reference in sales materials is 14 days (you have that) but for streaming sessions we sometimes keep a short-lived session cache (up to 6 hours) to support reconnection. Otherwise looks good to send.

Sara — thanks, and good call Karthik on the telemetry note. Attaching the EU pilot plan and adding a short summary below that you can paste into your vendor assessment:

Short-summary (copyable):
- Request text (prompts/user messages): default retention 45 days (hosted); can be disabled for enterprise customers or moved to EU region during onboarding.
- Generated outputs (model responses): default retention 14 days; can be shortened or disabled with enterprise contract. Streaming session caches may persist up to 6 hours to support reconnections.
- Request metadata and anonymized telemetry: retained 180 days (metadata) and 365 days (aggregated telemetry); telemetry does not include user text.
- Opt-out tradeoffs: disabling text retention prevents request replay for debugging/regressions; support will need sanitized repros. Billing metadata remains unless specifically requested for deletion.
